author: Sydney Hoier
title: Driver in 2024 crash asks judge for shorter sentence - NewsBreak
text:
By Sydney Hoier ,
4 hours ago
SIOUX FALLS, S.D. (KELO) — Damion Laurelez admits to speeding through a central Sioux Falls neighborhood, crashing into a house and killing two of his teenage passengers. Tests showed he had alcohol and drugs in his system.
But Laurelez says he does not deserve the sentence that a judge handed down. Despite a plea deal recommending no more than 30 years, Judge Douglas Barnett sentenced him to 40 years. Tomorrow, Laurelez will return to court in hopes of getting that sentence reduced.
Laurelez wrote in a handwritten letter to the judge that he understands that he received a longer sentence because of “what you were told was said on my phone calls.”
During the sentencing hearing, a police officer told the judge about a jail phone call. He said Laurelez told his mother he couldn’t show remorse in court or he’d laugh.
LifeQuest opens micro homes for independence in Mitchell In the letter, Laurelez admits making those statements but says they were not in the same sentence.
He also writes that he was raised to hide his feelings- something Laurelez claims he learned from his father, whom he never saw cry.
Since being in prison, Laurelez writes that he has a new outlook on life after hearing from inmates who are there for life sentences.
Laurelez is currently serving a 40-year sentence – 20 years for each of his victims. Milana Reeves and Eric Hopkins were 15 years old when they died.
KELOLAND News will be in the courtroom and will bring you a full report Thursday night.
